newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 92 people die in New Delhi fever.
newsitem.headline: At least 92 people die in New Delhi fever.

text.p: At least 92 people have been killed in an outbreak of dengue fever that has infected hundreds in India's capital, doctors and government officials said on Wednesday.
Patients have been admitted to about 28 hospitals in New Delhi. There have been no reports of the disease outside the capital so far.
Dengue, also called breakbone fever, is normally accompanied by high fever, headaches and pain in muscles and joints. It runs its course in six to seven days.
Delhi's health ministry officials said that more than 1,500 people have been infected with dengue since the first death was reported on August 29.
Dengue is usually carried by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water, especially in air coolers and other water-filled objects in residences in New Delhi.
Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court on Tuesday criticised the Lt Governor of Delhi and the state's health minister, Dr Harsh Vardhan, for slackness in dealing with the epedimic.
"The conscience of this court is alarmed at the way the death toll is increasing and on the slackness and indifferent attitude of the authorities concerned," said Justice Usha Mehra.
But Vardhan said the Delhi government had already warned it would take action against people in whose homes the Aedes aegypti mosquitoes were found.
